title: Polyploid newts build normal tubules by switching molecular mechanisms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Polyploid newts build normal tubules by switching molecular mechanisms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Engineered polyploid newts with much larger cells keep kidney tubule diameter normal by using fewer cells and, with truly enormous cells, a single cell bending around itself, showing that tissues call up different molecular mechanisms (cytoskeletal bending instead of cell–cell communication) to reach the same anatomical goal state.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This requires using a different molecular mechanism (cytoskeletal bending instead of cell–cell communication of tubulogenesis)—calling up different modular subroutines to accomplish their high-level goal state as needed, while circumstances (indeed, their inner components) change unexpectedly34.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “4. Beyond the Brain: Bowties Everywhere”. Scope: Polyploid newt kidney tubules

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The morphological prediction is precise and can distinguish the stated mechanisms. Existing published images may support only partial remeasurement, with uncertain sample coverage and no known complete open dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate ploidy and cell size to tubule diameter, cell count around the lumen, junctional organization and cytoskeletal geometry in newt kidney sections. Normal diameter with fewer cells and single-cell wrapping at extreme size supports mechanism switching; proportional enlargement or preserved multicellular construction refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Digitized raw microscopy and sample-level metadata may be unavailable.

The key observations come from historical experiments.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9
data existence: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell size, cell number, and tubule diameter were measured across ploidy series and can still be compiled from those papers, which covers the anatomical half of the claim for newts. The further statement that the tissue switches from cell-cell communication to cytoskeletal bending is a mechanism read off the histology, without a molecular dataset that would distinguish those subroutines. The anatomical part is partly checkable; the mechanism switch is not.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In polyploid newt kidneys, measure tubule diameter against ploidy, cell size, and cells per cross-section, and record whether the largest cells form a tubule by bending around themselves. Conserved diameter with falling cell number would support the anatomical claim; diameter scaling with cell size would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cytoskeletal bending versus cell-cell signalling is inferred from cell geometry, not from molecular markers.

The measurements are mid-twentieth-century histology tables, not a modern repository.

The record is limited to salamander kidney tubules.

fields.label: Dimension scores

discriminating power: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.8
